subject: Request: SLA scope exclusion for third-party tool-calls causing intermittent latency
messages:
From: Jared Mills <jmills@nimbus.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@nimbus.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary SLA exclusion for tool-call-induced latency

Hi Soojin,

Quick context: over the last 3 weeks our production traffic through Redwood has seen sporadic 2–6s tail latencies aligned with a third-party fraud check that we call synchronously (FraudX). When FraudX is slow the overall request exceeds our strict response window. Our security/compliance team requires those fraud calls remain inline for auditability, so we can't move them asynchronous without additional regulatory sign-off.

Can Redwood propose a short-term carve-out/exclusion so that delays caused by downstream FraudX timeouts are not counted against the SLA while we implement mitigations? Procurement is CC'd to keep timelines tight — we need contract language by COB next week. I've attached a sample log bundle and timestamps where we saw spikes.

Attachments: nimbus-fraud-call-logs-20261130.zip (logs, 2.3MB)

Thanks,
Jared
Head of Platform Ops
Nimbus Financial

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jmills@nimbus.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, procure@nimbus.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 17:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA exclusion for tool-call-induced latency

Thanks Jared — got the logs and appreciate the details. Looping in Karthik for commercial and Marissa for contract language / legal review.

We have two quick asks so we can scope the exclusion and propose precise language:
- Can you indicate the percentage of requests that hit FraudX (approx 95th pct vs overall)?
- Are there observable timeouts (e.g., >3s) or error codes we should enumerate in the exclusion clause?

Operationally we can support a time-bounded exclusion that excludes third-party synchronous tool-call latencies (FraudX) from Redwood's per-request p95 SLO calculation — provided we get: (a) clear definition of the error/time threshold, (b) a mitigation plan with target completion date, and (c) shared traces/logs for the exclusion period for audit.

I'll draft a short amendment once Karthik and Marissa confirm the approach. Suggest we propose an initial 90-day exclusion and re-evaluate earlier if fixes are deployed.

--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jmills@nimbus.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, procure@nimbus.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 18:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA exclusion for tool-call-induced latency

Jared — appreciate the quick signal and the log bundle. From a commercial standpoint we can do the following carve-out structure:

Option A (recommended): 90-day SLA exclusion window where Redwood excludes timeouts attributed to synchronous third-party tool-calls from p95 latency calculations. Conditions:
- Exclusion applies only when Redwood's trace shows the request blocked waiting on an external service call (FraudX) and the external call duration exceeds 500ms.
- Nimbus must provide weekly shared traces and a mitigation roadmap (milestones + ETA).
- Redwood will provide a temporary 5% bill credit cap if the exclusion correlates with >=2 production incidents in a 30-day window.

Option B: Shorter 30-day exclusion while Nimbus deploys async/queue fallback. No automatic credits; manual review for incidents.

We prefer Option A if your ops team can commit to weekly traces. If you want, we can draft amendment language and a short mutual action plan. Marissa — can your team prepare a minimal amendment template we can run to DocuSign?

Karthik
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Jared Mills <jmills@nimbus.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@nimbus.com
Date: Sat, 06 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA exclusion for tool-call-induced latency

Thanks Karthik — Option A looks reasonable. Confirming:
- We'll surface weekly traces by Monday morning (TZS) and include concrete milestones for moving FraudX off the synchronous path.
- 500ms threshold is acceptable; we'll flag timeouts >500ms as exclusion triggers.
- The 5% credit cap is fine as a backstop.

Please send the amendment draft and the mutual action plan. Procurement would like the DocuSign link and a succinct summary of the exclusion clause to attach to the PO.

Jared

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Mills <jmills@nimbus.com>, procure@nimbus.com
Date: Sat, 06 Dec 2026 10:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA exclusion for tool-call-induced latency

Thanks — drafting amendment now. Draft outline attached (slo-exclusion-proposal.pdf) — it includes:
- Precise exclusion language: "Delays attributable to synchronous third‑party tool calls (identified as external service calls in Redwood traces) exceeding 500 milliseconds shall be excluded from Redwood's p95 latency SLO for the period 2026-12-06 to 2027-03-06, provided weekly traces and a remediation plan are supplied by Customer."
- Audit requirements and data retention (30 days of traces retained for review).
- Billing fallback and 5% credit cap language.

I'll upload the DocuSign-ready amendment (amendment-draft.docx) and send a single-line summary for procurement to attach to their PO.

On a final note for internal tracking: we should tag this as a temporary SLA scope exclusion and ensure the rollout team (runtime-eng) is aware to avoid automatic incident crediting.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: slo-exclusion-proposal.pdf, amendment-draft.docx
